# `Scanner/BandFree-v0` · Keep the dark bands of two balanced SSFP images off their marked regions

**D · Image quality and artefacts** · artefacts · kind 2, set · isolates D14: Dark bands of balanced steady-state images. [The map](../../docs/tasks.md)

**Status:** ADMITTED: on 300 fresh instances per level the reference passes >= 96 %, no policy that ignores the object passes more than 4 % (95 % bounds)

What a frequency scout is for. The dark bands of balanced SSFP repeat every 1 / TR in frequency; where the marked regions fall in that pattern depends on the field, on the error of the frequency adjustment, on the material (oil sits 3.4 ppm below water) and on the repetition time, and how wide a band is depends on the material and on the excitation. The target is a 2D image: the slice profile of the selective pulse adds spins at smaller flip angles, whose signal peaks next to the band, so the band is narrower than the hard-pulse formula says and a band model has to carry the slice profile (a 3D acquisition with a hard pulse costs a multiple of the scan time and shows another band). A low bandwidth gives the least noise and the longest repetition time. The answer, for each of the two images, is the lowest bandwidth at which one phase cycle keeps every region clear of the bands with a margin for frequency drift, or the recognition that no single acquisition can, and then the pair of phase cycles that does. By level: level 1 is a measurement task, level 2 is a measurement task, level 3 is a measurement task (a fixed list of scans with a fixed estimator passes this many points below the reference: -1 at level 1, -0.7 at level 2, -0.3 at level 3; 300 instances per level; 25 points or more make a decision task).

Kind of task: **measurement** (reference minus open_loop, points of pass rate: -1 at level 1, -0.7 at level 2, -0.3 at level 3 (n = 300 per level, engine mrgym-engine-0.3.0)).

## World

- On the table: QA phantom (a disc of gel with vials; at level 3 one vial of oil), 3 T, field spread drawn per instance
- Sequences that matter here: bssfp, spgr
- Formulas the agent is given: phase per TR = 360 x off-resonance x TR - phase cycle; steady-state signal of bssfp as a function of that phase, integrated over the slice profile of the documented pulse (datasheet); off-resonance = phase slope of a multi-echo spgr

| Hidden (measurable only by scanning) | Told |
|---|---|
| the off-resonance field and its spread | the target images and the allowed bandwidths |
| the error of the frequency adjustment (up to 150 Hz) | the regions of each image |
| T1 and T2 of every material (they set the width of its band) | the three pass rules with every number |
| which marked region holds oil, and that one does (level 3) | the instrument datasheet (it gives the selective pulse) |
| transmit gain and B1 pattern | realised protocol, timing and cost of every plan and scan |
| whether one acquisition can be band-free |  |
| the 128-bit world seed |  |

## Deliverable and reward

- Deliverable: `submit` with `{'A': {'bandwidth_hz_per_px': '<60 to 600; level 3: from 90>', 'phase_cycle_deg': '[<one or two angles>]'}, 'B': {'bandwidth_hz_per_px': '<60 to 600; level 3: from 90>', 'phase_cycle_deg': '[<one or two angles>]'}}`
- Reward range [0.0, 1.0]; paid only at submit; 0 on every other step
- Gates: the scanner log replays and is within budget; at least one accepted scan; the console accepts the target scan of each image at the delivered bandwidth
- Error: `1 - the smallest kept fraction over images, regions and drifts (signal / signal at the region's best phase cycle)`
- Score: `none: the reward is 1 for a pass and 0 otherwise`
- Passing: all gates and, for each image: every region keeps >= 80 % at every drift up to -/+ 20 Hz; two acquisitions only if no single acquisition up to 400 Hz per pixel is band-free; bandwidth <= 1.15 x the lowest band-free bandwidth (comparison protocols: band-free up to 26 Hz of drift)

~~~text
# Keep the dark bands of two balanced SSFP images off their marked regions
A test object with vials of unknown materials lies in the field of
view. The examination needs two balanced SSFP images of it, image A and image B, each with a protocol of its own:
    sequence bssfp, flip_deg 60, matrix 120, field of view at the console default, slice 5 mm with the console's
    default slice-selective pulse, 1 average, bandwidth_hz_per_px of your choice between 60 and 600, tr_ms at the console
    minimum for that bandwidth (a plan shows it), phase_cycle_deg of your choice
No dark band may cross the marked regions of an image (circles; centre and radius in mm from the isocentre; each lies
inside one homogeneous material):
  image A
  R1: y -56.45, x -0.58, radius 6
  R2: y -14.01, x -54.52, radius 6
  R3: y 42.2, x 31.85, radius 6
  image B
  R4: y -18, x 51.22, radius 6
  R5: y 44.87, x -30.16, radius 6
Deliver with `submit`, for each image, the bandwidth and one phase cycle. If no single acquisition can keep every
marked region of an image out of the bands, deliver for that image the bandwidth and two phase cycles: two
acquisitions that differ only in the phase cycle. Every region is then read from one of the two, the one that shows
it better, and rule 1 must hold for it in that one.

Passing, for each image, all of:
1. Band-free, with a margin. Every marked region of the image keeps at least 80 % of the largest signal it can have
   at this bandwidth and repetition time (its signal at its best phase cycle). This must hold at the present centre
   frequency and at every drift of the centre frequency of up to 20 Hz either way (the same drift everywhere in the
   object).
2. No more acquisitions than needed. Two acquisitions pass only when no single acquisition at a bandwidth of 400 or
   less is band-free for that image.
3. Low bandwidth (the noise of the image grows with the square root of the bandwidth). The delivered bandwidth is at
   most 1.15 times the lowest bandwidth at which a band-free protocol with the same number of acquisitions exists
   for that image.
For rules 2 and 3 the scanner compares with protocols that stay band-free up to a drift of 26 Hz, so a protocol
that only just exists does not count against you.

The target images are not acquired in this episode: the scanner evaluates the protocols you deliver, noise-free.
Your own scans may use any sequence and any parameters the console accepts; only the deliverable is evaluated, on the scan the task names. That scan is not charged to the scan-time budget and not limited by it.
Nothing about the materials, the field or the frequency adjustment is known in advance. The scanner's log must show that you measured. An answer in the wrong unit is wrong.
~~~

## Determinism and versions

same (seed, level, tool calls) -> same observations, log hash chain and reward; a repeated scan draws new noise; the verifier's scans are noise-free.

Rewards are comparable only within one environment version (the `-vN` suffix) and one scanner engine (`mrgym --version`).
